title: 01. Fundamentals: WEAKREF, GC & MEMORY MANAGEMENT (Deep)
summary: Defines: Node, ExpensiveObject, on_finalize(), ImageCache, RegularPoint, SlottedPoint

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- GARBAGE COLLECTION — How Python Manages Memory
- 1. Reference Counting (Primary mechanism)
- When refcount reaches 0, memory is freed IMMEDIATELY
- 2. Cyclic Garbage Collector (For circular references)
- Reference counting can't handle circular references:
- The cyclic GC detects and breaks these cycles.
- Generation 0: Newly created objects (collected most frequently)
- Generation 1: Survived one collection

**Defines:** `Node`, `ExpensiveObject`, `on_finalize()`, `ImageCache`, `RegularPoint`, `SlottedPoint`

```python name=advanced/memory_management.py
# ============================================================
# GARBAGE COLLECTION — How Python Manages Memory
# ============================================================
import gc
import sys
import weakref
import ctypes

# ============================================================
# 1. Reference Counting (Primary mechanism)
# ============================================================
a = [1, 2, 3]
print(sys.getrefcount(a))  # 2 (a + getrefcount argument)

b = a
print(sys.getrefcount(a))  # 3 (a + b + getrefcount argument)

del b
print(sys.getrefcount(a))  # 2

# When refcount reaches 0, memory is freed IMMEDIATELY

# ============================================================
# 2. Cyclic Garbage Collector (For circular references)
# ============================================================
# Reference counting can't handle circular references:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None

# Circular reference!
a = Node(1)
b = Node(2)
a.next = b
b.next = a  # Cycle! Refcount never reaches 0.

# The cyclic GC detects and breaks these cycles.
del a, b  # Not immediately freed — GC will handle it

# --- GC Controls ---
gc.collect()               # Force garbage collection
gc.disable()               # Disable automatic GC
gc.enable()                # Enable automatic GC
print(gc.get_threshold())  # (700, 10, 10) — generation thresholds
gc.set_threshold(1000, 15, 15)  # Tune thresholds

# --- GC Generations ---
# Generation 0: Newly created objects (collected most frequently)
# Generation 1: Survived one collection
# Generation 2: Long-lived objects (collected least frequently)
print(gc.get_count())  # (count_gen0, count_gen1, count_gen2)

# --- Detect memory leaks ---
gc.set_debug(gc.DEBUG_LEAK)
gc.collect()
print(gc.garbage)  # Objects that couldn't be freed

# ============================================================
# 3. Weak References — Don't prevent garbage collection
# ============================================================

class ExpensiveObject:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"ExpensiveObject({self.name})"
    def __del__(self):
        print(f"Deleting {self.name}")

# --- Strong reference keeps object alive ---
obj = ExpensiveObject("strong")
strong_ref = obj
del obj  # Not deleted — strong_ref still holds it!

# --- Weak reference allows GC ---
obj = ExpensiveObject("weak")
weak_ref = weakref.ref(obj)
print(weak_ref())     # ExpensiveObject(weak)
del obj               # "Deleting weak" — object is freed!
print(weak_ref())     # None — object is gone

# --- Weak reference with callback ---
def on_finalize(ref):
    print(f"Object was garbage collected! Ref: {ref}")

obj = ExpensiveObject("callback")
weak_ref = weakref.ref(obj, on_finalize)
del obj  # Triggers callback

# --- WeakValueDictionary (cache that doesn't prevent GC) ---
class ImageCache:
    def __init__(self):
        self._cache = weakref.WeakValueDictionary()
    
    def get(self, path):
        img = self._cache.get(path)
        if img is None:
            img = self._load_image(path)
            self._cache[path] = img
        return img
    
    def _load_image(self, path):
        return ExpensiveObject(f"Image:{path}")

# --- weakref.finalize (Python 3.4+, preferred over __del__) ---
obj = ExpensiveObject("finalizer")
weakref.finalize(obj, print, "Cleanup triggered!")
del obj  # "Cleanup triggered!"

# ============================================================
# 4. Memory Profiling Tools
# ============================================================

# --- sys.getsizeof ---
print(sys.getsizeof([]))           # 56 bytes (empty list)
print(sys.getsizeof([1, 2, 3]))   # 120 bytes
print(sys.getsizeof({}))          # 64 bytes
print(sys.getsizeof("hello"))     # 54 bytes

# --- tracemalloc (built-in memory tracer) ---
import tracemalloc

tracemalloc.start()

# ... your code ...
data = [list(range(1000)) for _ in range(100)]

snapshot = tracemalloc.take_snapshot()
top_stats = snapshot.statistics("lineno")
for stat in top_stats[:5]:
    print(stat)

current, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
print(f"Current: {current / 1024:.1f} KB, Peak: {peak / 1024:.1f} KB")
tracemalloc.stop()

# ============================================================
# 5. __slots__ — Memory optimization for many instances
# ============================================================
class RegularPoint:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

class SlottedPoint:
    __slots__ = ('x', 'y')
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

# Memory comparison
print(sys.getsizeof(RegularPoint(1, 2).__dict__))  # 104 bytes
# SlottedPoint has no __dict__ — saves ~40-50% memory per instance
# For 1 million objects, this is significant!
```
